fields.features_heading: What Goes Into Your Real Estate Client Survey
fields.features_subheading: Name the stage of the sale and who reads the answers. Emergent builds the survey, its database, and alerts, all changed by prompt.
fields.feature_1:
A survey for each stage of a sale

Name the moment to ask about, like the week after closing or an open house walk-through. Emergent drafts questions for it, and you reword, add, or cut any by prompt.
fields.feature_2:
Answers filed by client and address

Each response saves as a row in a database you own, with the client, the address, and the agent on the deal. Pull one agent's closing ratings for the year in a single query.
fields.feature_3:
Low ratings land with the broker

Pick a floor, like communication under 4 out of 5. The app emails the managing broker, or posts in Slack, with the client's comment. Ratings above it go to the quarterly report.
fields.feature_4:
Built for a phone at the front door

Clients and open house visitors answer one question per screen, from an email link or a QR code by the entry. Emergent sets no cap on responses, for 12 groups or 120.
fields.feature_5:
Answers that reach your CRM

The app can send each response to the CRM your team already runs, through that tool's API. A buyer's budget and move date sit on the contact record before the agent calls.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Clients open the survey on your brokerage's own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. Paid plans also export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Brokerages Act on Client Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
Three low ratings, and all of them name inspection week

Ruskin Hollow Realty sends clients 6 questions 7 days after closing, and 41 of 54 answered last quarter. Any communication rating under 4 out of 5 goes to the managing broker, Odile Penhallow, the day it arrives. Three did, and all 3 comments named inspection week. She set a same-day reply rule for it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Open house answers reach the sellers by Monday morning

At the Sunday open house for 37 Wrenwick Lane, visitors scan a QR code at the door and answer 4 questions by phone. The home is listed at $612,000. Of 26 groups, 15 called the price high for the size, and 21 named the kitchen a strength. Corbin Wexley, the listing agent, sent the sellers that summary Monday morning.
fields.tab_content_3:
Buyers moving within 60 days go to the top of the call list

Before the first call, Beaumont Ferry Homes sends each new buyer an intake survey on budget, bedrooms, commute, and move date. Last month, 31 buyers answered. The 8 planning to move within 60 days went to the top of Liesl Corran's call list with budget and must-haves attached. She reached all 8 the next morning.
fields.tab_content_4:
One check-in a year after closing finds 9 possible sellers

A year after closing, Pellridge Real Estate sends past clients 3 questions, ending with how long they plan to stay. This year, 88 of 212 answered. Of those, 61 plan to stay 5 years or more and 18 are unsure. The 9 who may sell within 2 years went to agent Cass Pemberton as a call list.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Real Estate Client Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a real estate client survey that clients finish on a phone and that ends in a follow-up call.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what each answer will change
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about one thing per question
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask for the overall rating last
fields.howto_step_1_des: Before drafting a question, write down what a low answer should set off: a call from the broker, a price talk with the sellers, a place on the call list. Cut any question that sets off nothing. Put those triggers in your prompt, and Emergent builds the survey around them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Split "How were your agent's communication and negotiation?" into two questions. Pew Research Center calls questions that ask respondents to evaluate more than one concept double-barreled. Two separate ratings tell the broker which skill an agent needs coaching on.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Rate communication and pricing advice on the same 1 to 5 scale, with 5 as the best, and use it for every other rating too. A 3 from a buyer then means the same as a 3 from a seller, and this year's ratings line up against last year's without any conversion.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask about pricing advice and communication before asking how the whole sale went. Pew Research Center has found that the order in which questions are asked can influence how people respond. Keep the order the same for every client and every agent.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Before the first real client gets the link, have 2 past clients answer it on their phones. Pew Research Center calls pretesting an essential step in the questionnaire design process. Reword any question either of them asked you about, and check that each answer saved with the right address.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send it from the agent's own address
fields.howto_step_6_des: Clients know their agent, not the brokerage's no-reply inbox. Send the link from the agent's email with one line on why you are asking, and send a single reminder 5 days later to anyone who has not answered. Close the survey after 2 weeks.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Review ratings by agent each quarter
fields.howto_step_7_des: Every quarter, sort the ratings by agent and by stage of the sale, and pick the 1 or 2 lowest scores to coach on. Ask the same questions the next quarter, and the new scores show whether the coaching changed anything for clients.

faq_plan.q: What is a real estate client survey?
faq_plan.a: A real estate client survey is a short questionnaire an agent or brokerage sends buyers and sellers at a fixed point in a sale. It rates the agent's service and asks what the client plans next, from a move date to a referral.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a real estate client survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the survey in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder: when it goes out and who should hear about a low rating. Emergent builds the survey, the database behind it, and the alerts, and you change any question by prompting again. The free tier covers building and publishing.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a real estate client survey ask after closing?
faq_plan.a: Six questions cover it: a 1 to 5 rating each for communication, pricing advice, and responsiveness, an overall rating, whether the client would refer the agent to a friend, and one comment box. Name the agent and the property address in the invitation, so the client knows which sale the questions are about.

faq_plan.q: What should a real estate client survey measure besides satisfaction?
faq_plan.a: Measure what the client plans next: a move date, a budget, how long they expect to stay, and whether they would refer the agent. Those answers put a name on a call list, and a rating alone never does. When the rating is all you need, a customer satisfaction survey is the shorter build.

faq_plan.q: Should a real estate client survey ask buyers and sellers different questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for the ratings tied to each side's job. NAR found that home sellers want an agent to help them market their home for sale, price it competitively, and sell it within a specific time frame. Buyers want help to negotiate, explain, and understand the real estate market. Rate those tasks per side, and keep shared questions identical.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a real estate client survey have?
faq_plan.a: Keep a post-closing survey to 6 questions or fewer and an open house survey to about 4, since visitors answer while standing at the door. If no one on the team will act on a question's answer, cut it before the survey goes out.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more clients to answer a real estate client survey?
faq_plan.a: Tell clients at the closing table that a short survey is coming, then send it on the day you named. Let them answer on a phone: Emergent builds conversational surveys that show one question per screen. The same habits fit any customer feedback survey: say who reads the answers, and later, what changed because of them.

faq_plan.q: Should clients give their names on a real estate client survey, or answer anonymously?
faq_plan.a: Ask for names after closing and at intake, since a low rating only helps if the broker can call that client back. Say in the invitation who reads the answers. An open house survey can skip names, with an optional email field for visitors who want updates on the listing. With Emergent, each named answer sits in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can I use real estate client survey answers as testimonials?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once the client says you may. Put a yes-or-no question right after the comment box asking whether you may quote it with their first name and town, and publish only comments marked yes. Store that answer next to the comment, so anyone on the team can check it before a quote goes on the website.

faq_plan.q: Should a real estate client survey ask how the client found the agent?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as one multiple-choice question: a friend or relative, an agent they used before, an online search, a yard sign, or something else. NAR found that buyers and sellers were happy with their agent and would recommend or use them again. This answer shows how much business returns that way. To learn who in your area knows the brokerage at all, run a brand awareness survey.

plan.angle: The SERP for this keyword is thin and mixed (land-survey questions, generic survey apps, template lists). No result shows what an agent or brokerage does with a client's answer. This page shows four real estate client surveys built from a prompt, each placed at one moment of a sale and each ending in an action: a low communication rating after closing reaching the managing broker, open house answers on price reaching the sellers the next morning, buyer intake answers putting near-term movers at the top of an agent's call list, and a one-year check-in turning up past clients who may sell. The how-to gives question-design advice backed by Pew Research Center, with NAR findings on what buyers and sellers want from an agent, and the FAQ answers what a builder asks: what to ask after closing, timing, length, anonymity, testimonials, CRM sync, and how clients found the agent.

At a Sunday open house at 37 Wrenwick Lane, listed at $612,000, visitors answer 4 questions on their phones from a QR code at the door; 26 groups answer, 15 of 26 call the price high for the size, and the listing agent, Corbin Wexley, sends the sellers the summary Monday morning.

Beaumont Ferry Homes sends new buyers an intake survey before the first call (price ceiling, bedrooms, commute, move date); 31 buyers answered last month, and the 8 who plan to move within 60 days go to the top of agent Liesl Corran's call list with their answers attached.

Pellridge Real Estate sends past clients a 3-question check-in one year after closing; 88 of 212 answered, 61 plan to stay 5 years or more, 18 are unsure, and 9 may sell within 2 years, and those 9 go to agent Cass Pemberton as a call list.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Real Estate Client Survey for Buyers and Sellers', meta title 'Real Estate Client Survey Builder for Agents | Emergent' and hero 'Build a real estate client survey that asks at each stage of a sale, flags low ratings to your broker, and keeps answers you own.' state the whole job; how-to description is one sentence on what the steps achieve.

intent.evidence: Thin, mixed SERP; page gives the question set ('Six questions cover it: a 1 to 5 rating each for communication, pricing advice, and responsiveness, an overall rating...'), a 7-step how-to, and four stage-by-stage examples (post-closing, open house, buyer intake, past clients) matching the meta promise.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'inspection week', 'listed at $612,000', 'managing broker', 'a QR code by the entry', 'how long they plan to stay'; table column uses the survey variant.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Name the moment to ask about...', 'Ruskin Hollow Realty sends clients 6 questions...', 'Before drafting a question, write down what a low answer should set off...'.

craft.evidence: QC Q5 at 2 ', so' endings (under the block line); sentences vary; no blocking craft defect. Notes recorded on FAQ 10's 'This answer' reference.

voice.evidence: Reads as an operator's page: 'Cut any question that sets off nothing.', 'Clients know their agent, not the brokerage's no-reply inbox.' Repeated ideas recorded as notes.

truth.evidence: Pew quotes (double-barreled, question order, pretesting) and NAR quotes (sellers 'market their home for sale, price it competitively, and sell it within a specific time frame'; buyers 'negotiate, explain, and understand the real estate market'; 'happy with their agent and would recommend or use them again') match domain_sources spans and the live NAR page, scope kept, no percentages invented. Emergent sentences map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, conversational, no-caps, api-connect, custom-domain, code-export, free-start. Tab 4: 61 + 18 + 9 = 88 of 212; tab 2 shares 15/26 = 58%, 21/26 = 81%, 6/26 = 23%. No licensing or fair-housing advice; intake asks budget, bedrooms, commute, move date only.

distinct.evidence: Real-estate-only stories and steps; sibling primaries (customer satisfaction survey, customer feedback survey, brand awareness survey) appear only as FAQ links, never as headings.
